messages:
Oncall Bot: [ALERT] Canary cluster for inference-service (eu-west-1) reporting increased 5xx rate and latency spike. Trigger: error-rate > 2% for 3m. Pager -> @alex @maria @pat
Alex: saw the alert. just pulled the canary dashboard — tailing logs now. errors look like OOM-ish + `invalid kv-cache` on some requests.
Maria: deploying a model variant yesterday at 11:18 UTC — could be model binary mismatch w/ runtime. tagging @SRE Lead for infra impact.
Pat: paging in. traffic shift was 10% to canary, ~30 RPM. customer-facing? any hits from big tenants?
SRE Lead: Ops metrics show ~1200 requests in the last 10m to the canary. A handful of customers show increased latencies (per-route). Recommend immediate safe-mode: scale canary to 0 and route traffic back to main.
Alex: agreed. preparing rollback. quick check: `kubectl get deploy inference-service -n prod -o yaml | grep annotations -A2`
Alex: deploy-bot shows rollouts: main (revision 53), canary (revision 54).
Maria: I'll flip the feature flag to prevent new traffic to canary: `flagctl set inference.canary.enabled false --env=prod`
Jordan: I'm running the rollback command to revert the deployment to revision 53. posting commands I'll run:
```
# revert canary subset
kubectl -n prod scale deploy inference-service-canary --replicas=0
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=53
```
Pat: note — manual rollback may not undo DB migrations, but last deploy didn't include schema changes. double-check migration logs.
Alex: confirmed no migrations. the model artifact path changed, but main uses the previous artifact.
Ops Bot: deploy task queued: rollback to rev 53 requested by Jordan. CI checks: health-checks + smoke.
Maria: flipping routing rules in gateway now to remove canary pool. `gatewayctl set-backend inference-service canary=false`
Alex: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T10:41:22Z ERROR inference runtime: failed to load kv-cache: checksum mismatch
2026-03-15T10:41:23Z WARN model-loader: falling back to unoptimized kernels
2026-03-15T10:41:24Z ERROR request handler: OOM while allocating 128MB
```
SRE Lead: these look like model artifact/serialization mismatch causing memory blowouts. rollback seems right. also oncall: create post-rollback smoke checklist: 1) 5xx rate back to baseline 2) p95 latency under SLO 3) no elevated memory eviction events 4) confirm top customer routes healthy.
Pat: I'll call out to CS for customers with active sessions (cc @Jordan).
Jordan: rollback started — rolling update in progress (5 pods). monitoring health endpoint: `/healthz` and tokenized smoke: `curl -sS https://inference.prod/healthz | jq .status`
Alex: rolling update finished. health checks passed on all pods.
Ops Bot: automated canary autoscaler disabled for 20m as mitigation.
Maria: running smoke tests against the main pool now (sample prompts + long-form). posting sample test output: `latency median 80ms, p95 290ms, error-rate 0.08%`
SRE Lead: good — 5xx back to baseline. Observability trace shows requests now hitting revision 53 exclusively.
Pat: CS update: no active customer escalations so far; intermittent errors may have affected a few developers, but we have no confirmed data loss.
Alex: note for postmortem: investigate artifact publish pipeline — checksum validation should have caught this. possibly a race between model packaging and artifact index update.
Maria: agreed. immediate follow-ups: (a) block new model rollouts until checksum validation is enforced (b) add a canary runway with gradual probe-based ramping (c) add evictions OOM alarms to canary metrics.
Jordan: handing oncall to Maria for the 30-min post-rollback watch. I'm stepping off primary.
Maria: taking primary. will monitor metrics and take full postmortem writeup. cc @SRE Lead — please collect kernel logs from affected pods: `kubectl logs -l app=inference-service --since=30m`
SRE Lead: will grab logs and dump to the incident bucket. also schedule a quick sync with model owners to trace artifact SHA.
Pat: thanks team. I'll update the incident record with customer impact = "degraded for a subset of canary traffic, no confirmed retries lost, no db migration impact" and severity -> P2 pending postmortem.
Alex: adding a short mitigation note for runbook: if future canary shows memory/kv-cache errors -> immediately scale canary to 0, rollback to last stable revision, and notify CS.
Ops Bot: Incident closed (manual mitigation applied). Follow-up tasks created: TASK-4872 (artifact checksum), TASK-4873 (canary ramp improvements), TASK-4874 (OOM alarm tuning).
Maria: thanks all. I'll own the postmortem and aim to have a draft in 48h.
Jordan: ending shift, thanks. :thumbsup:
